# Error codes

Every failure is a `BluetoothClassicError` with one of these `code` values, on both platforms.
Compare against the exported `ErrorCode` constants:

```ts
import { ErrorCode, isBluetoothClassicError } from '@dynlabs/react-native-bluetooth-classic';

try {
  await connect(address);
} catch (error) {
  if (isBluetoothClassicError(error, ErrorCode.CONNECT_TIMEOUT)) {
    // retry later
  }
}
```

Besides `code` and `message`, an error can carry `platform`, `deviceId`, `connectionId`,
`missingPermissions`, `nativeCode` and `nativeMessage`. `JSON.stringify(error)` includes all of them.

## Setup and adapter

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `MODULE_NOT_LINKED` | The native module is not registered in this build. | Rebuild the app after installing or upgrading the package. Expo Go is not supported; use a development build. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_ON_PLATFORM` | The current platform or OS release cannot perform the operation. | Check `getCapabilities()` before calling platform-specific APIs. iOS has no discovery, pairing, server sockets or adapter state. |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | An argument or option is missing, unknown, of the wrong type or out of range. | The message names the offending argument or option key. Option keys are camelCase; v1 keys such as `DELIMITER` are rejected. |
| `BLUETOOTH_UNAVAILABLE` | The device has no Bluetooth hardware. | Hide Bluetooth features on this device. |
| `BLUETOOTH_DISABLED` | Bluetooth is switched off. | Ask the user to turn Bluetooth on, for example with `requestEnable()` on Android. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | A runtime permission required by the operation is not granted. | `missingPermissions` lists what is missing. Call `requestPermissions(scope)` first. |
| `LOCATION_SERVICES_DISABLED` | Android 7-11 (API 24-30) only returns discovery results while Location Services is switched on. | Ask the user to switch on Location Services, then retry discovery. |
| `USER_REJECTED` | The user declined a system prompt or dismissed a picker. | Explain why the action is needed before asking again. |
| `ACTIVITY_UNAVAILABLE` | No Android activity is in the foreground to show a system prompt or screen. | Call the API while the app is in the foreground. |
| `UNKNOWN` | An unexpected failure with no specific mapping. | Inspect `nativeCode` and `nativeMessage`, and report the issue with debug logs. |

## Discovery and pairing

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` | The requested device or accessory could not be found. | Make sure the device is powered on, in range and discoverable. |
| `DISCOVERY_ALREADY_RUNNING` | A discovery session started by the library is already running. | Wait for the running session to finish, or call `cancelDiscovery()`. |
| `DISCOVERY_FAILED` | The OS refused to start discovery. | Retry after a short delay; check `nativeMessage` for the OS reason. |
| `PAIRING_IN_PROGRESS` | A pairing started by the library for the same device is still pending. | Await the pending `pair()` call. |
| `PAIRING_FAILED` | Bonding ended without a bond, or the OS refused to start bonding. | The user may have declined or entered a wrong PIN. Retry, or pair from system settings. |
| `PAIRING_TIMEOUT` | Bonding did not finish within the timeout. | Increase `timeoutMs` or retry with the device closer. |

## Connections and data

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `CONNECT_FAILED` | The connection attempt failed. | `nativeMessage` carries the OS reason. On Android, try `android.transport: 'insecure'` or `android.fallbackChannel`. |
| `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | The connection attempt did not complete within the timeout. | Make sure the device is in range and accepts connections, or increase `timeoutMs`. |
| `CONNECT_CANCELLED` | The connection attempt was cancelled through its abort signal. | No action needed. |
| `ALREADY_CONNECTED` | A connection to the same target already exists. | Use `getConnection(error.connectionId)` to reuse the existing connection. |
| `ALREADY_CONNECTING` | A connection attempt to the same target is already pending. | Await the pending `connect()` call. |
| `NOT_CONNECTED` | The connection has already ended. | Connect again before writing. |
| `CONNECTION_LOST` | The connection ended because of an unexpected local failure. | Reconnect; inspect `nativeMessage` if it keeps happening. |
| `ACCEPT_FAILED` | Listening for incoming connections failed. | Check `nativeMessage`; another app may be listening on the same service. |
| `ACCEPT_TIMEOUT` | No device connected within the accept timeout. | Call `accept()` again, or increase `timeoutMs`. |
| `ACCEPT_CANCELLED` | The pending accept was cancelled. | No action needed. |
| `ACCEPT_ALREADY_RUNNING` | Another accept is already pending. | Await the pending `accept()` or call `cancelAccept()`. |
| `WRITE_FAILED` | The OS reported an error while writing; the connection has ended. | Reconnect and resend. |
| `WRITE_TIMEOUT` | A write was not fully accepted within its timeout; the connection has ended. | The remote device stopped reading. Reconnect and resend. |
| `READ_TIMEOUT` | No frame arrived within the read timeout. | The connection stays open; retry the read or resend the request. |
| `BUFFER_OVERFLOW` | Received data exceeded the configured buffer limit. | Attach a data listener or reader sooner, or raise `maxBufferBytes` / `maxFrameBytes`. |

## iOS accessories

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `PROTOCOL_NOT_DECLARED` | The protocol is not listed in UISupportedExternalAccessoryProtocols. | Add the protocol to Info.plist (or the config plugin's `protocols` option) and rebuild. |
| `PROTOCOL_NOT_SUPPORTED` | The accessory does not support the requested protocol. | Use one of the accessory's `protocolStrings`. |
| `ACCESSORY_NOT_CONNECTED` | The accessory is not currently connected to the OS. | Accessory ids change on every reconnect; call `getConnectedAccessories()` again. |
| `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` | The OS refused to open a session with the accessory. | Another app may hold the session, or the accessory rejected it. Check `nativeMessage`. |
